Correlation between body appreciation an.evidence_source: Girls: “There was a weak negative relationship between the BAS-2 and BMI in the three countries; however, this relationship was significant in Portugal (r = .14, p = .015), but not in Denmark (r = .19, p = .117) or Sweden (r = .15, p = .077), which may be due to the larger sample size in Portugal.” Boys: “The relationship between body appreciation and BMI for boys was also less clear, as a weak negative relationship was found in Portugal (r = −.33, p < .001), but there was no statistically significant relationship either in Denmark or in Sweden.” Note: reported text describes a 'weak negative relationship' for girls but the reported r coefficients for girls are positive; extracted the reported r values as given.
Correlation between body appreciation an.warning: Text describes negative relationship for girls but reports positive r coefficients for girls (inconsistency).

Number of studies.evidence_source: The section reports convergent validity results across samples in Denmark, Portugal, and Sweden within a single study context: “Convergent validity was assessed by looking at the correlations ... for boys and girls in Denmark, Portugal, and Sweden separately.”

section_summary.extract_value: This section reports convergent validity analyses of the BAS-2 across adolescent samples in Denmark, Portugal, and Sweden, examining correlations with self-esteem, psychological well-being, intuitive eating, and BMI separately for boys and girls. For girls a weak relationship between BAS-2 and BMI is described and reported as significant only in Portugal (r = .14, p = .015) but not in Denmark or Sweden; for boys a weak negative relationship was found in Portugal (r = −.33, p < .001) but not in the other countries. The section references Tables 5–7 and Supplementary Tables 3 and 4 and notes generally similar patterns across countries.
